title: Establish WHY the second conflicting_assertion branch in _apply_assertions is dead, and pin which guard actually answers the conflict
objective: PR #110 reported the second conflicting_assertion refusal in HtmlDocAdapter._apply_assertions as STRUCTURALLY DEAD but its instrumentation was temporary and is gone, so nothing standing in the tree establishes why. This slice constructs the input that OUGHT to reach that branch, demonstrates what actually happens to it, identifies WHICH refusal answers it, and classifies the deadness against the three candidate explanations (impossible by construction / wrong call path / upstream defect silently collapsing a conflict).

verdict.case: Dead by DOMINATION from a co-located guard. NOT the upstream-mechanism story, and NOT an upstream defect.
verdict.case_3_excluded: The constructed conflicting input is REFUSED, not swallowed: one candidate, verification_state='rejected', error='conflicting_assertion', detail="field='offer_type'", and no extracted facts survive on the rejected candidate.
verdict.case_1_premise_corrected: The brief's case 1 asks for an UPSTREAM mechanism guaranteeing one assertion per field. There is none. HtmlExtractionProfile.__post_init__ (apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/html.py lines 194-288) neither deduplicates assertions by field nor rejects two assertions on one field; it normalises text and scope and validates the field vocabulary and the verbatim rule only. A profile carrying two offer_type assertions with different values constructs successfully and reaches the loop.
verdict.actual_mechanism: Branch A (line 984, 'assertion.field in facts and existing != assertion.value') DOMINATES branch B (lines 991-994). Line 1002 'facts[assertion.field] = assertion.value' executes unconditionally in the same loop iteration immediately after line 1001 'asserted_fields[assertion.field] = assertion.value', so the invariant 'for every f in asserted_fields, facts[f] is asserted_fields[f]' holds at the top of every iteration. B's predicate is therefore the same comparison on the same operands as A's, restricted to a subset of keys, and A is evaluated seven lines earlier.
verdict.consequence: The INTENT the branch encodes -- two assertions disagreeing about one field must refuse the document -- is fully enforced, by branch A. This is a redundant refusal, not an unprotected intent. That distinction is the whole finding: a reader who sees the check and concludes the case is covered is correct, just about the wrong line.

what_this_slice_is_not: It is NOT a repair and NOT a deletion. apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/html.py is byte-identical to base, proved by git blob hash bcde62bf4051dd27b9062a7002dbae7e13a878b1 before and after every mutation.
It does not mark any feature passing. agent-state/feature_list.json is untouched (blob 154de1fef2ba).

It does not touch .github/workflows/ci.yml, scripts/check_urls.py, tests/unit/test_url_allowlist.py, .secrets.baseline, either lockfile, or tests/integration/test_catalogue_currency.py (a parallel slice owns that file).
No npm install / i / update / audit fix was run. This slice touches no JavaScript.
No database was needed or created: every experiment is pure in-process extraction against an in-memory fixture fetcher.
in_scope: Construct the assertion-vs-assertion conflict input and record what actually happens to it.
Measure WHICH _rejected() call site refuses it, by call site rather than by error string (the two refusals emit the identical string, so the error alone cannot distinguish them).
Classify the deadness against the three candidate explanations and name the mechanism with its lines.
ADD tests that pin the CURRENT relationship between the two branches. No production behaviour change.
out_of_scope: Removing the dead branch. The brief licenses deletion only on a proved upstream mechanism, and there is none; html.py is also a mandatory Level-2 category where a change to what an evidence-extraction path accepts or refuses is an owner decision. PR #110 declined for the same reason and its handoff recommended exactly this owner decision as a separate slice.
Changing what any guard matches, accepts or rejects.

method.primary_instrument: MUTATION plus a call-site probe. A name-grep answers 'who calls this symbol', not 'what guards this behaviour'. Because both refusals emit the identical error string 'conflicting_assertion', no behavioural assertion on the error can tell them apart -- the discriminator has to be the call site.
method.call_site_probe: HtmlDocAdapter._rejected is wrapped and the CALLER's frame line number recorded (inspect.currentframe().f_back.f_lineno). Expected line spans are derived from the AST of the module under test, never from a hardcoded literal, so the probe follows the source if it moves. No sys.settrace, so nothing fights a coverage tracer.
method.instrument_negative_control: Before trusting any 'branch A answered' result, the same probe was driven at a DIFFERENT refusal (assertion_not_found) and observed to report that site (line 966) rather than A's (line 985). Without this, a probe hardwired to A's line would have confirmed exactly what was hoped.
method.every_mutation_restores_the_original_def: Each mutation deletes a guard entirely -- the hole as it would exist if the guard had never been written -- rather than breaking arity or an argument. Each mutated tree was checked with 'ruff format --check' and 'ruff check' (exit 0 for all three) so that a formatting nit could never turn a top-line conclusion red for a reason unrelated to the product.
method.which_guard_killed_it: Killing test node ids recorded per mutation, so a kill by a pre-existing guard is never accepted as evidence for the branch under test.
method.baseline_shown_to_have_executed: Targeted baseline: 134 collected, 134 passed, exit 0, over tests/unit/test_adapter_html_conflict.py + test_adapter_html_assertions.py + test_adapter_html_matrix.py, recorded before any edit. pytest exit 5 is treated as NOTHING COLLECTED.
method.environment_precondition_asserted_not_an: Python 3.13.15 and pytest 9.0.3 read from the interpreter; 'import app.ingest' executed and observed to succeed before any experiment. No coverage plugin is configured in pytest addopts, checked in pyproject.toml.
method.predictions_recorded_first: All eight predictions were written to a file before the first experiment ran. One MISSED and is reported.

acceptance_criteria: The constructed assertion-vs-assertion input is exhibited, together with what actually happens to it, at the pristine base commit.
The refusing call site is identified by measurement, not inference, and the probe is shown able to report a different site.
Branch B is shown to be FUNCTIONAL rather than merely unexecuted, by removing branch A and observing B answer the same input.
The counterfactual is exhibited: with both guards removed, the conflicting document is ACCEPTED carrying the last assertion's value, which is what the pair prevents.
The mechanism is named with its lines, and the brief's case-1 premise is either confirmed or corrected against the source.
No production file changes; byte-identity proved by git blob hash.
Added tests fail when the relationship they pin is broken -- shown by re-running the branch-A mutation with the new tests present.
Errors made during the slice are reported as prominently as the verdict.

verification_method.database: None required. No container was created, so none needed removal.
commands: python -m ruff check . && python -m ruff format --check .

migration_and_data_implications: None. No schema change, no migration, no production write.

security_privacy_portability_z0.security: No security boundary touched. No guard weakened, suppressed or relaxed; the guard under study is unchanged.
security_privacy_portability_z0.portability: No dependency added or changed. Neither lockfile touched.
security_privacy_portability_z0.z0: Material to the extent that _apply_assertions stands between a contradicted field and publication. The counterfactual measured here shows precisely what the pair of guards prevents: with both removed, a document whose two pinned assertions disagree is ACCEPTED carrying offer_type='trial' from the last assertion, which on this product is an accepted-but-contradicted field and a route to an unsupported free claim. Branch A prevents it today; this slice changes nothing about that.

regression_risks: The added tests are pure additions; no existing test was modified or weakened.
The added tests monkeypatch HtmlDocAdapter._rejected through pytest's monkeypatch fixture, which restores it after each test, so no global state leaks between tests.

The added tests anchor branch identity to the PREDICATE each refusal sits under (facts vs asserted_fields), read from the AST, rather than to line numbers or to source order, so an innocuous reordering does not produce a false alarm and a removal of branch A does not silently satisfy them.
required_evaluation_level_reason: The code under study is a provider adapter and evidence-extraction path, a mandatory Level-2 category. No behaviour is changed, but the CLAIM that a refusal in that path is unreachable is exactly the kind of claim an independent evaluator must re-derive, and the recommendation that follows from it (whether to delete the branch) is an owner decision.
hard_rules_acknowledged: No feature marked passing; agent-state/feature_list.json untouched.

WHAT SHOULD HAPPEN IF BRANCH A IS EVER WEAKENED: not answered. It was measured that branch B would then become the live guard -- a branch that has never executed. Whether that is acceptable cover is a design question this slice did not decide.

THE DOMINATION ARGUMENT IS OVER THE CURRENT FUNCTION BODY. It was not proved for values with pathological __eq__ in general. What was established is narrower and is the claim actually supported: both predicates compare the SAME stored object against the SAME operand with the SAME operator, because lines 1001 and 1002 assign one value to both dicts in the same iteration, so no asymmetry between the two predicates is possible.

WHETHER A REAL PROVIDER PAGE COULD PRODUCE THIS CONFLICT: measured only over committed configuration. 35 HTML profiles are registered, 31 declare at least one assertion, and ZERO declare the same field twice, so no committed profile can produce an assertion-vs-assertion conflict today. That is a statement about the profiles in this repository, not about what a future author might write.
